newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real closes up 0.01 pct in calm trading.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real closes up 0.01 pct in calm trading.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.01 percent to close at 1.0191 against the dollar in calm trading in the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
The Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0190 real per greenback to drain excess dollars from the market in the late afternoon.

Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Thursday deficit of $10 million. But dealers said the Central Bank still needed to drain the large supply of dollars remaining from Wednesday's $161.4 million surplus.
"Banks that held dollars from Wednesday decided to sell them today," one trader said.
Dealers said the market continued expecting a drop in the real-dollar mini-band in coming days. The current mini-band was set on Tuesday between 1.019 and 1.024 reais per dollar.
In the interbank forex floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0241 to the dollar, up 0.08 percent, after the Central Bank sold dollars at 1.0240 per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real ended flat at 1.037 per greenback, traders said.
